query: What is the primary follow‑up timing relative to intervention start and what is the primary causal estimand (ITT)? How will complier/PP/LATE be defined and instrumented?

response.query: What is the primary follow‑up timing relative to intervention start and what is the primary causal estimand (ITT)? How will complier/PP/LATE be defined and instrumented?
response.answer: Primary follow-up timing is typically immediate post-intervention. The primary causal estimand is the intention-to-treat (ITT) effect. Compliers/PP/LATE are defined as those who follow the intervention protocol; they are instrumented using regression discontinuity or instrumental variable approaches.

results.title: Designing digital health interventions with causal inference ...
results.content: # Designing digital health interventions with causal inference and multi-armed bandits: a review This paper provides an overview of the advancements, challenges, and future directions in translating principles of lifestyle medicine and behavior change into AI-powered mobile health (mHealth) applications, with a focus on Just-In-Time Adaptive Interventions. Bayesian multi-armed bandits from reinforcement learning are exploited as a framework for tailoring interventions, with causal inference methods used to incorporate structural assumptions about the user’s behavior. Along with structural goal-setting, the psychological mechanisms behind motivation and habit formation should also be considered for digital health interventions design (23). Microrandomized trial design for evaluating just-in-time adaptive interventions through mobile health technologies for cardiovascular disease.
